name: isInputsSource
summary: Whether `file` is one of the game's sources the check reads: not a test, whose fixture games are not shipped.

name: isOrientationSource
summary: Whether `file` is one of the game's sources the check reads: not a test, whose fixture games are not shipped.

name: ITCH_FIRST_PUSH_CHECKLIST
summary: The one-time page settings butler cannot make (PUB spec §6), printed after a channel's first push.

name: ITCH_LIMITS
summary: itch.io's documented limits for an HTML5 upload; "MB" is read as 10^6 bytes.

name: ITCH_LIMITS_SOURCE
summary: Where itch.io's limits were read, and when.

name: ItchBuildInvalid
summary: The build breaks one of itch.io's rules; each problem names the file and the limit.

name: ItchCheck
summary: The `prepare --target itch` check that failed, in the order they run (PUB spec §4).

name: ItchConfig
summary: What a game writes in `ship.config.ts`.

name: itchConfigSchema
summary: Checks a game's `itch` section: `project` is `user/game` in lower case, and `channel` defaults to `html5`.

name: ItchSettingMissing
summary: `publish --target itch` lacks the config section, the key or butler; found before anything runs.

name: ItchSettings
summary: The checked settings, with the channel filled in.

name: keysBindingsIn
summary: What the `keys()` calls in one source file bind, one `<file>:<line>:<col> keys` entry per call (and `pad` and `gestures` entries where it binds them); empty when the file has no call; `undefined` when it does not parse (its typecheck already fails, and a half-read tree could name a device that is not there).

name: ManifestInputsMismatch
summary: `runtime.inputs` disagrees with the game's input bindings (M4 spec §4.13, I-g).

name: ManifestInvalid
summary: Ruken's parser refused the generated `ruken.toml`.

name: OrientationMismatch
summary: The game plays in an orientation its ship config's `runtime.orientation` does not send Ruken (M4.7 follow-up).

name: OrientationMismatchFound
summary: A game that plays in an orientation its ship config does not declare.

name: parseEnvFile
summary: The variables of one `.env` file: `KEY=value` lines, with `export`, quotes and `#` comments allowed.

name: PlayedOrientation
summary: An orientation a `defineGame` call plays in, at the literal's opening quote (or at the call, when it is left out).

name: portsFor
summary: The ports a checkout's test server and preview build listen on (FloorFifty `playwright.config.ts`).

name: prepareBuild
summary: Makes a built folder ready for `ruken publish` and the dev host (ship spec §3.3): checks the tag, the entry page, root-absolute paths, secrets (QB-b), the leaderboards the game names (M5.7) and the orientation it plays in (M4.7) and the devices its `keys()` calls bind (M4.1), then writes `ruken.toml` once Ruken's parser accepts it.

name: PrepareInput
summary: What `prepareBuild` checks and writes into: the built folder, the ship config, and the optional release tag, game folder and input bindings.

name: prepareItch
summary: Makes a built folder ready for itch.io (PUB spec §4): the tag, root-absolute paths, secrets (QB.2: a page on itch.io is public, so the build is scanned as Ruken's is), `index.html`, itch.io's limits, reference case and a stray `ruken.toml` are checked in that order, and the first that fails stops prepare before anything is written.

name: PrepareItchInput
summary: What `prepareItch` checks and zips: the built folder, the ship config and the release tag.

name: ProcessError
summary: A program could not be started (not found, not executable).

name: PublishAuth
summary: Exit 3: the token was missing, wrong or lacks the rights.

name: PublishFailed
summary: Any other exit code.

name: PublishInput
summary: What `publishToRuken` needs: the prepared build folder, the game's folder, Ruken's site and token, and whether to activate the build.

name: PublishItchInput
summary: What `publishToItch` needs: the built folder, the ship config, the tag, the key and where butler is.

name: PublishRejected
summary: Exit 1: Ruken's checks rejected the build.

name: PublishTimeout
summary: Exit 4: Ruken's checks took longer than the CLI waits.

name: publishToItch
summary: Prepares the build for itch.io (every check of `prepareItch`), then pushes the folder with butler.

name: publishToRuken
summary: Runs Ruken's own `ruken publish` on a prepared build and returns the URL Ruken says the build is served at (`undefined` when it prints none).

name: PublishUsage
summary: Exit 2: the command line was wrong.

name: readEnvValues
summary: The variables of every top-level `.env*` file in the game folder; none when the folder does not exist.

name: RootAbsoluteReference
summary: The build names its own files from the origin's root, which 404s under `/b/<buildId>/`.

name: rukenCliPath
summary: The `ruken` bin of the vendored `@ruken/cli` package.

name: rukenToml
summary: The text of `ruken.toml` (Ruken manifest schema 1) for a ship config.

name: scanTextForSecrets
summary: Every secret in one file's text.

name: SecretFound
summary: A secret the bundle scan found in a built file, located without repeating the secret.

name: SecretInBuild
summary: The build holds a key, an `.env` value or a high-entropy string (QB-b).

name: SHIP_PACKAGE
summary: The name this package is published under.

name: ShipConfig
summary: What a game tells ship about itself, in Ruken's own manifest shape (`@ruken/manifest`'s `Manifest`).

name: ShipInputBindings
summary: What ship reads of a game's input profile.

name: testRemote
summary: Pushes the current branch, dispatches CI for it, waits and returns the run's URL and one `<result>\t<job>` line per job when it is green.

name: TestRemoteFailed
summary: `test-remote` stopped without a green run; `reason` says why and `message` says what to do.

name: TestRemoteInput
summary: What `testRemote` runs and how long it waits.

name: TestRemoteReason
summary: Why `test-remote` stopped without a green run.

name: UndeclaredBoard
summary: The game names a leaderboard its ship config's `leaderboards` does not declare (M5 spec §4.8, L-b).

name: UndeclaredBoardFound
summary: A board the game's sources name that its ship config does not declare, at the call site.

name: VersionMismatch
summary: A release tag that is not `v<version>`.

name: canonicalJson
summary: Canonical JSON: object keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace.

name: CanonicalJsonError
summary: A value canonical JSON cannot represent exactly; hashing it anyway would let different values collide.

name: Command
summary: Input to the sim (spec §4.4 rule 4).

name: CommandDef
summary: A command the sim accepts as input: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match.

name: CommandRecord
summary: A command as a system reads it this tick: the player slot that sent it (`source`), its per-source `seq` and its parsed `payload`.

name: ComponentDef
summary: A component: a stable id and a flat record of typed fields.

name: createRng
summary: A generator seeded from `seed` (through splitmix32): the same seed gives the same sequence in every engine.

name: createSim
summary: Creates a sim from its plugins, seed and content; async, because a plugin may create engine state (a Rapier world).

name: Def
summary: Anything `definePlugin`'s flat `defs` list takes (DX spec §3.2).

name: defineCommand
summary: Defines a command by id and payload schema.

name: defineComponent
summary: Defines a component from an id (lower-case words separated by dots or dashes) and its fields by name and type.

name: defineEvent
summary: Defines an event by id and payload schema, to emit from a system with `ctx.emit`.

name: definePlugin
summary: Defines a plugin from a name, its dependencies and its definitions, given in the keyed lists or in one flat `defs` list sorted by kind.

name: defineResource
summary: Defines a resource by id, schema and starting value.

name: defineSystem
summary: A system: `defineSystem(name, run)` runs in `gameplay`, `defineSystem(name, phase, run)` in that phase, and the object form also takes `before`/`after`.

name: deriveSeed
summary: Seed for a named substream: FNV-1a over the name's UTF-16 code units, mixed with the root seed.

name: EntityRef
summary: A live entity, addressed by its StableId.

name: EventDef
summary: An event a system emits: an id and the Zod schema its payload must match.

name: FieldRecord
summary: One component's field values on an entity, by field name.

name: FieldSchema
summary: A component's fields, by name.

name: FieldType
summary: A component field's type: `f32`, `f64`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `entity` (a StableId, stored as a `u32`) or `string`.

name: FieldValue
summary: The JavaScript type a field holds: `boolean` for `bool`, `string` for `string`, `number` for every other type.

name: FieldValues
summary: The writable record of values a `FieldSchema` describes.

name: hex64
summary: 16 lowercase hex digits.

name: Phase
summary: One of the six phases a tick runs through, in `PHASES` order.

name: PHASES
summary: Fixed phase order (spec §4.3).

name: PluginDef
summary: A bundle of definitions the sim registers together: components, commands, events, resources and systems, the plugins it depends on, and optionally per-sim engine state and `config`.

name: PluginState
summary: Engine state a plugin keeps outside the ECS, such as a Rapier world (M2.1 spec §3.1).

name: PluginStateSetup
summary: What a plugin's state may know when it is created.

name: PreparedRestore
summary: A plugin's parsed restore, held until the sim knows whether the whole snapshot is valid.

name: RejectedCommand
summary: A command `step` dropped, with the reason.

name: RejectReason
summary: Why `step` dropped a command: `bad-header` (a field is missing or out of range), `unknown-command` (no plugin defines its type), `wrong-tick` (not the sim's current tick), `duplicate-seq` (the same source and seq twice in one step) or `invalid-payload` (it fails the command's schema).

name: RenderDelta
summary: What changed for the renderer since the last delta (spec §4.7).

name: RenderRow
summary: One entity's render-flagged components (component id -> field values).

name: ResourceDef
summary: A value the sim keeps once, not on any entity: an id, a Zod schema and the `init` that gives its starting value.

name: Rng
summary: A deterministic generator (xoshiro128**, 32-bit integer math only, so it is bit-exact in every engine).

name: RngState
summary: The four 32-bit words of a generator's state, as `Rng.state()` copies them and snapshots store them.

name: Sim
summary: A running simulation, stepped with commands, that can snapshot, restore and hash its state.

name: SIM_VERSION
summary: The sim package's version, written into replay headers for information only (M2.3 spec §3.2).

name: SimCapacityError
summary: More sims are alive than Koota allows worlds (16 per process).

name: SimContext
summary: What a system's `run` receives each tick (spec §4.1).

name: SimDisposedError
summary: The sim was disposed; it holds no world any more, so every call that reads or changes state refuses.

name: SimEvent
summary: An event a system emitted during a step: the event's id as `type`, and its parsed `payload`.

name: SimFaultedError
summary: A system threw during `step`.

name: SimOptions
summary: What `createSim` takes: the root `seed`, the `plugins`, `tickHz` (an integer from 1 to 1000, default 60) and the `content` the systems read as `ctx.content` (default `{}`).

name: SNAPSHOT_VERSION
summary: The snapshot format version this build reads and writes; a snapshot of another version fails with `SnapshotFormatError`.

name: SnapshotFormatError
summary: Snapshot bytes that are not a valid snapshot of this format version: bad magic, an unsupported version, truncated or malformed sections.

name: SnapshotMismatchError
summary: A valid snapshot that belongs to another sim: `field` names the header value that differs (`schemaHash`, `contentHash` or `tickHz`), with this sim's `expected` value and the snapshot's `actual` one.

name: SnapshotView
summary: A readable copy of a snapshot, for diffs and reports (M2.3 spec §3.1).

name: sortedEntries
summary: Own enumerable [key, value] pairs, sorted by key.

name: sortedKeys
summary: Own enumerable string keys, sorted by UTF-16 code unit.

name: SpawnPart
summary: A component to spawn with: the definition alone (defaults) or [definition, initial values].

name: StepResult
summary: What one `step` produced: the new tick, the events emitted, the renderer's delta and the commands that were rejected.

name: SystemDef
summary: A system: a name, the phase it runs in, the systems it must run `before` or `after` within that phase, and its `run`, called once per tick.

name: SystemSpec
summary: The object form of `defineSystem`: a name, a phase, the optional `before`/`after` ordering and the run.

name: xxhash64
summary: XXH64 of `data` with an unsigned 64-bit `seed`.

name: canonicalJson
summary: Canonical JSON: object keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace.

name: hex64
summary: 16 lowercase hex digits.

name: utf8
summary: UTF-8 encoding without TextEncoder (the sim's lib has no DOM/Web APIs).

name: xxhash64
summary: XXH64 of `data` with an unsigned 64-bit `seed`.

name: atan
summary: Deterministic arctangent.

name: atan2
summary: Finite inputs only (sim values are finite).

name: cos
summary: Deterministic cosine, in radians.

name: exp
summary: Deterministic `e` to the power `x`.

name: hypot
summary: No overflow scaling: inputs must satisfy x*x + y*y < 1.7e308.

name: log
summary: Deterministic natural logarithm.

name: pow
summary: Deterministic `x` to the power `y`.

name: sin
summary: Deterministic sine, in radians.

name: tan
summary: Deterministic tangent, in radians, as `sin(x) / cos(x)`.

name: createRecorder
summary: Starts recording `sim` from its current state, for the recorder's `step` to extend.

name: createReplayStepper
summary: Creates a stepper over `replay`: a fresh sim built from the replay's seed and tick rate, restored from its start snapshot.

name: decodeReplay
summary: Decodes `.replay` bytes (already inflated) into a `Replay`.

name: DEFAULT_CHECK_EVERY
summary: How often, in ticks, a recording stores a check hash when `RecorderOptions.checkEvery` is not given.

name: encodeReplay
summary: Encodes a replay as `.replay` bytes before deflate.

name: packReplay
summary: Encodes a replay and deflates it into `.replay` file bytes.

name: Recorder
summary: Steps a sim and records the run as a `Replay`.

name: RecorderOptions
summary: What a recording takes: how often to store a check hash, whether to keep a reference hash and snapshots (goldens), and free-form `meta`.

name: Replay
summary: A recorded run: its header, the start snapshot, the accepted commands by tick, check hashes along the way and the final tick and hash.

name: REPLAY_FORMAT
summary: The `.replay` format version this build reads and writes.

name: REPLAY_INFLATE_MAX_BYTES
summary: Larger than FloorFifty's 1 MiB because goldens carry reference snapshots; player replays may pass less.

name: REPLAY_MAX_TICKS
summary: The longest run a replay may hold: 2^24 ticks, over 77 hours at 60 Hz.

name: ReplayCheck
summary: A hash check at a tick: the hash the replay recorded (`expected`) and the hash the re-simulated sim has (`actual`).

name: ReplayCommand
summary: A command as a replay stores it: the sim's `Command` without its tick, which the replay's `ticks` entry carries.

name: ReplayCompression
summary: The deflate and inflate a `.replay` file needs.

name: ReplayFormatError
summary: Bytes that are not a valid `.replay` (M2.3 spec §5).

name: ReplayHeader
summary: The facts a replay needs before it plays: tick rate, seed, the schema and content hashes it was recorded against, where it starts and how often it checks.

name: ReplayRecordError
summary: A recording that cannot be exact: the sim stepped outside the recorder, a payload that is not JSON, and so on.

name: ReplayStepper
summary: A replay playing back one tick at a time on its own sim.

name: ReplayStepSetup
summary: What a stepper needs to rebuild the recorded sim: the same `plugins` and `content` the recording sim had.

name: unpackReplay
summary: Inflates `.replay` file bytes and decodes them.

name: documentScrolls
summary: The document itself never scrolls; screens scroll inside declared regions.

name: FakeResizeObserver
summary: Controls the fake `ResizeObserver` `installFakeResizeObserver` put in place: report a width to every observer, then restore the original.

name: fakeViewportWindow
summary: A fake window of the given size.

name: FakeViewportWindow
summary: A stand-in for the browser window the geometry owner reads: its size, `screen`, `navigator`, visual viewport and `resize` listeners, with methods to rotate, open the keyboard and count live listeners.

name: FakeVisualViewport
summary: The visual viewport of `FakeViewportWindow`: its height (less the keyboard, if open), an offset, and listeners for `resize`.

name: findClipped
summary: Each element `selector` names is tall enough for what it holds (a crushed row clips its content).

name: findCutAtSide
summary: No control is cut at a side of a declared scroll region that clips it (see `clippedBy`).

name: findIntrusions
summary: No visible control intersects a reserved area (Ruken's strip, a keyboard), in viewport px, by its whole box.

name: findOffscreenControls
summary: Every visible control is on screen, unless a declared scroll region (`[data-scroll-region]`) clips it (see `clippedBy`): a fixed control, or one positioned outside the region, is judged where it is drawn, since scrolling the region would never bring it into view.

name: findOverlaps
summary: Two elements' boxes do not overlap.

name: findSmallTargets
summary: Every visible control is at least `min` square, and a primary (`data-kind="primary"`) at least `minPrimary` tall.

name: findUnreachable
summary: Each element is fully inside the viewport, and the whole of it is in view: a tap at its centre and at the middle of each edge lands on it or inside it, so nothing covers or clips any part.

name: hostDisplay
summary: Ruken's display metrics for a hosted game.

name: installFakeResizeObserver
summary: Replaces the global `ResizeObserver` with a fake that reports only the widths you give it, for components measured under jsdom, which has no layout.

name: LayoutRect
summary: Layout assertions as plain DOM functions (M1.6 spec §3.10), from FloorFifty's `tests/e2e/support/layout.ts` at 122a220 (`expectReachable`, `expectControlsFit`, `expectRowsWhole`, `expectApart`, `expectNoDocumentScroll`).

name: MountedFixture
summary: A mounted Svelte fixture: the element it was mounted into and a way to unmount it.

name: mountFixture
summary: Mounts a Svelte component with the given props and no renderer or host, and flushes effects so the first render is finished.

name: pressedPart
summary: What a player presses for `control`: a checkbox's or radio's label (the theme draws it as the control, and a press anywhere on it toggles the input), else the control itself.

name: REFERENCE_SIZES
summary: The viewports a layout is checked at: phones in both orientations, tablets, desktops, both sides of every breakpoint and the tightest sizes, each with the classification it should get.

name: ReferenceFormFactor
summary: `@mcthaydt/automata-ui`'s `FormFactor`.

name: ReferenceHeightTier
summary: `@mcthaydt/automata-ui`'s `HeightTier`.

name: ReferenceSize
summary: One viewport every primitive and screen is checked at: a name, its size, and the form factor and height tier it must classify as.

name: textSnippet
summary: A Svelte 5 snippet rendering `<tag>text</tag>`, so a test can pass `children`, `body` or an icon to a component without writing a wrapper component (Ruken `packages/ui/src/test-snippets.ts`).

name: TIGHT_SIZES
summary: Sideways phones shorter than 780x270, where an open keyboard leaves the least room (framework audit of #7, 2026-10-11).

name: Variant
summary: A condition layered over a reference size.

name: VARIANTS
summary: The conditions each size is also checked under: at rest, with the on-screen keyboard open, with Ruken's reserved strip on the right or the left, and at its TV scale.

name: visibleControls
summary: Controls a player could see and reach: laid out, not hidden, not in an inert subtree.

name: Direction
summary: A direction on the D-pad or the stick.

name: Engine
summary: The browser engine a matrix cell runs in.

name: FakePad
summary: One standard controller in a real browser, driven through the Gamepad API the game itself reads.

name: FakePadOptions
summary: How the fake pad reports itself: its mapping and its id (the id picks the prompts' glyphs).

name: flick
summary: A quick vertical swipe of `dy` pixels within `ms` milliseconds from `from` (M4 spec I-f: 40 px in 180 ms).

name: hold
summary: A finger down on `target`'s centre until `until` resolves true (checked once a frame), then up.

name: INPUT_MATRIX
summary: M4 spec §9.1's cells, in table order: 17 cells, 22 journeys (the desktop cells run under both hosts).

name: InputDevice
summary: The device a matrix cell plays with.

name: MatrixCell
summary: One cell of the input × form-factor matrix: a form factor, a device and an engine, and the hosts it runs under.

name: MatrixFormFactor
summary: A matrix cell's form factor, each with one viewport (M4 spec §9.1).

name: MatrixHost
summary: Where a journey runs: under the fake Ruken host, or standalone.

name: PAD_BUTTONS
summary: The standard mapping's buttons by name: south (A on an Xbox pad) is 0, Start is 9, the D-pad 12 to 15.

name: PadButton
summary: A standard-mapping button by name.

name: PadMode
summary: Whether a direction is held on the D-pad or the left stick.

name: Point
summary: A point in the target frame's own CSS pixels.

name: swipe
summary: A finger from `from` to `to` over `ms` milliseconds, one move a frame, on whatever is under it.

name: tap
summary: A finger down on `target`'s centre and straight up again.

name: fakeGamepads
summary: `target` hears `gamepadconnected` and `gamepaddisconnected`, as `window` does in a browser.

name: FakeGamepads
summary: Four gamepad slots a unit test plugs pads into and presses; `getGamepads` reads them as the browser's would.

name: Difference
summary: One difference between two snapshot views: its kind, where it is (`entity 4 bounce.ball.vx`), the entity's sid when it is an entity, and both values as printed.

name: diffSnapshotViews
summary: Every difference between an expected and an actual snapshot view, field by field, in a fixed order (header, rng, resources, next id, entities, plugin bytes) so a report reads the same in every engine.

name: expectGolden
summary: Throws with the formatted report unless the golden matched or was just written.

name: formatGoldenReport
summary: One report as text: a line for most outcomes, and for a divergence the tick and up to 20 differences.

name: GOLDEN_MAX_PACKED_BYTES
summary: A golden that passes this cannot be reviewed or loaded cheaply; lower snapshotEvery's cost instead.

name: goldenCommands
summary: The Vitest browser commands that let golden tests read golden files in a browser: register them with `browser: { commands: goldenCommands() }`.

name: GoldenReport
summary: What a golden check found: `pass`, `written`, `missing`, `schema-changed`, `content-changed`, `setup-changed` or `diverged` (with the first differing tick and the fields that differ).

name: nodeCompression
summary: Node only.

name: replayGolden
summary: Replays a golden `.replay` against the current sim and reports whether it still matches.

name: ReplayGoldenOptions
summary: What `replayGolden` checks: the `.replay` file, the plugins and content to replay it with, and how to record it when updating goldens.

name: RoundTripFailure
summary: One case whose restored run differed from the uninterrupted one: its number, sim seed, length, restore tick, variant and a report of what differed.

name: RoundTripOptions
summary: What `snapshotRoundTripProperty` runs: the plugins, content and a command script, and how many cases of what length to try.

name: RoundTripVariant
summary: How a case restores: into a `fresh` sim, or into one that has `dirty` (stepped on past the snapshot).

name: simGolden
summary: Plays a scripted run and compares the sim's hash every `every` ticks with the golden JSON file, reporting the first recorded tick that differs.

name: SimGoldenOptions
summary: What `simGolden` runs: the plugins, content, seed and scripted commands to play for `ticks` ticks, where the golden JSON lives, and how often to record a hash.

name: snapshotRoundTripProperty
summary: Checks that snapshot, restore and continue equals an uninterrupted run, over many seeds, run lengths and restore points, alternating fresh and dirty restores.

name: streamCompression
summary: Browsers and Node: CompressionStream / DecompressionStream('deflate-raw').

name: goldenCommands
summary: The Vitest browser commands that let golden tests read golden files in a browser: register them with `browser: { commands: goldenCommands() }`.

name: GoldenCommandsOptions
summary: Options for {@link goldenCommands}.

name: RoundTripFailure
summary: One case whose restored run differed from the uninterrupted one: its number, sim seed, length, restore tick, variant and a report of what differed.

name: RoundTripOptions

name: ControlsCopy

name: ControlsSection

name: CornerControls

name: CursorInput

name: defaultSlot

name: DeviceClass

name: DisplayCopy

name: DisplayQuality

name: DragTracker

name: ErrorAction

name: ErrorCode

name: InputMethod

name: LanguageCopy

name: LeaderboardCopy

name: LeaderboardView
summary: What the panel shows: the rows, or why there are none.

name: LoaderOverlay
summary: The loader over a screen while its assets load (M1.6 spec §3.4; from FloorFifty `ui/components/LoaderOverlay.svelte` at 122a220).

name: lockOverscroll

name: pastEdge

summary: A portrait viewport narrower than this is a phone; at or above it, a tablet.

summary: Which fingers are down on which action.

name: RotateToastCopy
summary: The rotate toast's words (`rotateHint: 'toast'`, FloorFifty's): the advice, and its OK.

name: SaveSlots
summary: The save slots (M5 spec §6, §7): a row for each slot, and the few things a player does with one.

name: SaveSlotView

name: SaveStatusCopy
summary: One line per state, in the game's language (each a PRODUCT.L message key).

name: SaveStatusState
summary: What the host says about the player's saves, or that there is no grant.

name: SaveStatusTone
summary: How much a state asks of the player's notice.

name: ScreenFrame
summary: Every screen's frame: the visible region, a corner row, then a hero and a body (M1.6 spec §3.4; from FloorFifty `ui/layout/ScreenFrame.svelte` at 122a220).

summary: A list that keeps its rows (M1.6 spec §3.4; from FloorFifty `ui/layout/ScrollList.svelte` at 122a220).

name: scrollWithin
summary: Brings `element` into view by scrolling its nearest scroll box, never the document.

name: sendBack
summary: Sends Back as an Escape to wherever a dialog would hear it, and reports whether anything took it.

name: SettingsTab
summary: A tab of the Settings screen (FloorFifty's Settings and Controls): its label and its sections, in order.

name: SETTLE_DELAYS_MS
summary: When to measure again after a viewport event, in ms.

name: Sheet
summary: A Modal on the bottom edge at every form factor (M4 spec §4.12): the same scoping, Close and scroll region, where a thumb reaches the actions.

name: SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT
summary: At or below this many CSS px of layout height, a screen is short.

name: Sleeper
summary: Puts the game's sound to sleep while nobody can see it.

name: sleepWhenHidden
summary: Puts a game's sound to sleep while its page is hidden and wakes it when the page shows again; a pointer, touch or key gesture also asks sound the system suspended to resume.

name: Slider
summary: A number in a range (M4 spec §4.12): a labelled native `<input type="range">`, so the browser gives the arrow keys and the focus navigator's `adjust` steps it.

name: slotActionsOf
summary: What a player may do with a slot (M5 spec §6).

summary: Two panes side by side where both fit at `min` px, stacked otherwise (M4 spec §4.8; from FloorFifty `ui/layout/Split.svelte` at `ac72660`).

name: splitMode
summary: Split's choice (M4 spec §4.8; from FloorFifty `ui/layout/split.ts` at `ac72660`): side by side when both columns and the gap between them fit at their minimum, stacked otherwise.

name: STICKY_MARGIN_PX
summary: How far outside a button a thumb still counts for it, in CSS pixels.

name: StickyPointers
summary: Which button each finger is on, over the latch.

name: suppressPageGestures
summary: Turns off the browser's document gestures over the game.

name: SwipeIndicatorView
summary: What a SwipeSurface draws: the thumb, the anchor it trails and whether it is past the dead zone.

name: SwipeSurface
summary: The whole visible screen as one swipe surface (M4 spec §4.4), from FloorFifty `ui/components/SwipeSurface.svelte` at `ac72660`.

name: SwipeSurfaceProps
summary: SwipeSurface's props.

name: tabbables
summary: Everything Tab can reach under `root`, in DOM order: not disabled, inert or hidden.

name: tileSide
summary: A square tile's side for the space a grid is given: the width shared by the columns and the `peek` (a fraction of a tile) of the next page showing at the edge, and the height only when the box has one.

name: Timers
summary: Injected so tests drive the settle delays with fake timers.

name: Toast
summary: A passing message (M4 spec §4.12): "Pad connected", "Saved", "This controller is not supported".

name: Toggle
summary: An on/off setting (M4 spec §4.12): a native checkbox with the switch role, so the browser gives Space and the focus navigator's `adjust` flips it.

name: TouchButtonSpec
summary: One on-screen touch button (M4 spec §4.4): the action it holds and what it shows.

name: TouchControls
summary: The on-screen touch buttons (M4 spec §4.4), from FloorFifty `ui/components/TouchControls.svelte` at `ac72660`.

name: TouchControlsProps
summary: TouchControls' props.

name: TouchCopy
summary: Every word the Touch controls group shows, in the game's language.

name: TouchSection

name: TouchStickSpec
summary: The overlay's move stick (M4.12).

name: TouchTarget
summary: A button's action and where it is drawn, for `nearestTarget`.

name: trimRows
summary: The shape cut to the rows the largest group fills, so no page carries a row of empty slots.

name: UI_SLOT_NAMES
summary: The named places an extension may add UI (M1 shared contracts §2; M1.6 spec §3.7).

summary: What an extension puts in a slot: a Svelte component that takes no props.

name: UiSlotName
summary: The name of a place an extension may add UI: one of `UI_SLOT_NAMES`.

name: VibrationCopy
summary: Every word the Vibration group shows, in the game's language.

name: VibrationSection

name: ViewportWindow
summary: The parts of `window` the owner reads; a fake from `@mcthaydt/automata-testing` stands in for it in tests.

name: watchImage
summary: Probes `src` and, while it fails, hands `onRetry` each retry's URL to draw instead.

name: WheelPager

name: withHostName

name: wrapPage
summary: `index` wrapped into `0..count - 1`, so paging past either end comes round.

name: byTestId

name: checkLayout

name: errorPanelFloor

name: publishConditions

name: settleLayout
